heroHeadline: BLS April Jobs: +115K (Beat vs ~60K Consensus); Unemployment 4.3% Unchanged; S&P 500 ~7,395; Oil Brent ~$101 — Warsh Senate Vote 3 Days Away, Trump-Xi Summit May 14-15
heroSubtitle: May 8: The BLS April 2026 Employment Situation delivered a significant positive surprise — +115,000 nonfarm payrolls vs. the ~60K consensus, with unemployment unchanged at 4.3%. The beat reduces near-term recession risk: Goldman Sachs ~20% (from 22%), JPMorgan ~25% (from 28%), Moody's Analytics ~40% (from 42%). S&P 500 extended its Iran-ceasefire-driven rally to ~7,395 (+0.41% on May 8), building on May 7's +1.5% surge to 7,365 — Dow approached 50,000 for the first time as investors priced in both labor market resilience and Iran de-escalation. Oil continued its pullback: Brent ~$100.54 (May 8), WTI ~$91 — down from the $114-115 peak of May 5. US 10Y Treasury yield eased to ~4.32% (from 4.44% peak May 5) as the jobs data was interpreted as growth-supportive without inflationary enough to force the incoming Warsh Fed to hike. CRITICAL REVISION: February 2026 payrolls were revised deeper to –156,000 (from –133,000) — the deepest single-month loss since April 2020, reflecting the full impact of DOGE cuts and early Iran war business uncertainty. Initial jobless claims (released May 7): 200,000 (week ending May 2), below the ~205K consensus — labor market holding steady. Iran ceasefire: US 14-point MOU under Iranian review; Secretary of State Rubio 'waiting for a serious offer.' Both sides maintained the diplomatic pause. Kevin Warsh Senate floor vote expected as early as May 11-12 (~92% confirmation probability; Powell's term expires May 15). Trump-Xi Beijing summit remains on track for May 14-15. Section 122 tariff cliff July 23 (Congressional action required).
footerNote: Data sourced from BLS Employment Situation April 2026 (released May 8, 2026: +115K nonfarm payrolls, unemployment 4.3%), DOL Initial Jobless Claims (May 7, 200K week ending May 2), Federal Reserve H.15 (10Y yield ~4.32%), BEA Q1 2026 GDP Advance +2.0% (Apr 30), BLS CPI March 2026 (3.3%), BEA PCE March 2026 (3.5%/3.2% core), Federal Reserve FOMC (Apr 29 unanimous hold 3.50-3.75%), ISM Services PMI April 2026 (53.6 composite, Prices Paid 70.7 — highest since 2022), ADP April 2026 (+109K, pay +4.4%), RBA May 2026 (+25 bps to 4.35% — third consecutive hike), ECB (Apr 30 hold 2.00%), Bank of England (Apr 30 hold 8-1, 3.75%), BOJ (Apr 28 hold 6-3, 0.75%), Goldman Sachs Research (~20% recession probability), JPMorgan Global Markets Strategy (~25%), Moody's Analytics (~40%), Bloomberg (Trump-Xi summit confirmed May 14-15), CNN / Al Jazeera (Iran ceasefire talks continuing), TheStreet / 247WallSt (S&P 500 market updates), CNBC / EIA / IEA (oil prices Brent ~$100-101 May 8), Penn Wharton / CBP CAPE Portal ($166B IEEPA refunds), USTR Section 301 investigations (16 countries, hearing concluded May 5-8).
